answer_1.quote: Despite recent advancements, large language models (LLMs) are known to produce factually incorrect output. [...] Sports reporting is one such domain, and in this paper, we investigate the factual accuracy of LLMs for generating NBA game summaries. This is a challenging text generation task [...] We evaluate factual and semantic errors [...] and attributes (e.g., scores, time, period, distance). We hypothesise that structuring the complex play-by-play data is important for producing factually accurate summaries [...] generate paragraph-style summaries from complete play-by-play data [...]
datasets: NBA game play-by-play data from Basketball Reference

answer_4.quote: We manually annotated 3,312 errors across 180 play-by-play summaries generated for 30 NBA games [...] One of the authors manually annotated errors in all 180 generated summaries, and a second annotator independently annotated 9 summaries (5% of the dataset) to assess inter-annotator agreement. We provided detailed guidelines describing error categories, examples, and instructions for marking errors.
answer_4.guideline: manual error annotation protocol adapted from [and] refined with seven error categories: Number, Name, Word-objective, Word-subjective, Context, Not Checkable, and Other
